fact: The health ministry's e-Santé strategy states that the ministry has a Système National d'Information Sanitaire under its Direction des Statistiques, covering the whole country for the reporting of health data; the stocktake behind it was validated in September 2018.

The Stratégie Nationale E-Santé 2019-2023 carries project P121, strengthening and extension of the SNIS, in an action plan of 15 projects costed at USD 10 million (CFA 5,690,500,000) over five years, with funding still to be mobilised.

The strategy says the SNIS reports health data nationwide by electronic, semi-electronic and manual means, and that DHIS2, online since September 2016, has begun to be deployed in health facilities for data entry, in 'certain' facilities only.

The strategy gives no count of facilities entering data in DHIS2, saying only that deployment has begun in certain health facilities; it counts 1,026 integrated health centres and 2,443 health huts in the public network.
The strategy states that there is not yet a national electronic patient record project, only a few initiatives under way, and its 15-project action plan for 2019-2023 lists none.
The only electronic patient record activity the strategy reports is the digitalisation of two health districts, Gaya and Gothèye, of 72 districts; it gives no facility count.

The mid-term evaluation for Enabel (fieldwork 4 to 22 November 2024) states that the PASS Sutura project has set up digitalisation, including computerised medical records and billing, in the integrated health centres (CSI) and the district hospitals of its target health districts, Dioundiou, Gothèye and Gaya.

The evaluation places the digitalised health centres (CSI) in the project's three target health districts only, Dioundiou, Gothèye and Gaya, and gives no count of centres using the computerised medical record and no denominator.

The evaluation states the digitalisation is a flagship element of PASS Sutura, a Belgian bilateral project with EUR 14.5 million for health over 2022-2026, and that a Netherlands co-financing of EUR 3.2 million for 1 January 2023 to 31 March 2025 puts particular emphasis on digitalisation in the three districts; no domestic funding is stated.

The evaluation states the digitalisation initiatives were started by the Enabel project PASS Sutura with recruited consultancy firms, and describes the Ministry of Health's digital health directorate as involved and committed, with sustainability elements still being put in place.

The article states that Niger's DHIS2 system, which it describes as the national routine health management information system, is hosted within the Directorate of Statistics at the Ministry of Health; it gives no date for this, so the published date is used.

Enabel states that a hospital information system built around a computerised medical record was put in place at the district hospitals of Gaya and Gothèye after two field missions in February and April 2024, following a patient-record dematerialisation process begun in 2017.

Enabel places the hospital information system in two district hospitals only and says a mission planned for September 2024 will explore extending some of its modules to other facilities, notably urban integrated health centres and district pharmacies.

Enabel states that under its PASS Sutura programme it recruited an e-health consultancy in December 2022 to write the specification and retained the Post-Factum consortium to deploy the hospital information system at Gaya and Gothèye.
Enabel presents the hospital information system at Gaya and Gothèye as delivered within its health-system support programme PASS Sutura, launched in March 2022; no domestic funding is stated.

The health ministry's monitoring guide sets the circuit as: each health establishment fills a standard monthly activity report, validates it internally and keys it into DHIS2, the CSI entering its monthly report by the 15th of the following month and its notifiable-disease data each Monday; this is the prescribed procedure, not a measured practice.

The guide states that every health establishment, public and private, civil and military, keys its monthly report into DHIS2, naming integrated health centres (CSI) and hospitals as data sources without separating hospital levels, while health posts (cases de santé) and private structures send their data to their CSI by the 10th, where it is checked and keyed.

The monitoring and evaluation guide of the health development plan PDSS 2022-2026, issued by the health ministry, names DHIS2 as the base for managing routine health data and sets yearly targets to 2026 for SNIS report timeliness and completeness.

The guide makes the ministry's Direction des Statistiques responsible at central level for the monthly reports and for the SNIS timeliness and completeness indicators, with data management under the ministry's standard operating procedures manual.

The guide gives no count or share of CSIs keying their own reports; it gives, from the 2021 statistical yearbook, a CSI SNIS report completeness rate of 97.90% and a timeliness rate of 54.63% for 2021, defined as reports transmitted over reports expected, with targets of 100% and 75% by 2026.

The strategy places the SNIS under the health ministry's Direction des Statistiques, which it names as the institution responsible for coordinating project P121; no date is given, so the strategy's 2019 publication year is used.

The P121 project sheet recommends recourse to partners' financing, and the plan's financing table assigns USD 1.00 million of the project's USD 1.20 million to technical and financial partners and nothing to the health ministry's own column; this is planned financing, not a recorded budget.

The strategy describes the SNIS as currently semi-electronic, reporting by electronic, semi-electronic and manual means, with DHIS2, online since September 2016, used for data entry in certain connected health facilities only; no date is given, so the 2019 publication year is used.

The strategy gives no count of facilities entering data in DHIS2; project P121 sets a baseline of 0 and a target of more than 50% for the share of ministry structures (health centres, hospitals, regional directorates, districts, central departments) connected to the SNIS and feeding it automatically.

Component b of project P121 in the 2019-2023 strategy plans a standard management application for autonomous health structures (hospitals), building towards a national hospital information system, and states that the electronic patient record will be developed within that component; it is a plan, with no system yet in place.
